- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline to 1–2% below peak unless sentiment turns bullish.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 1.0) over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate future prices — apply mean reversion bias: subtract 2–3% from forecast if price > 1.5σ above recent 10-day average.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in early horizon (e.g., 1–7 days ahead) — increase forecast by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +2.0 to -2.0 in 3 days), model fails to adjust quickly — apply lag correction: shift forecast 1–2 days ahead by -0.5 to -1.0 units if sentiment turns negative.
